startup.name: Instinct
startup.description: A proactive team of AI agents that search thousands of markets, investigate opportunities and operate 24/7 for an individual trader, who acts as portfolio manager. Crypto and onchain markets are the starting point. Team of 5 in San Francisco, Winter 2026 batch.

yc_acceptance.basis: The company is already in the batch that starts on the as of date, so this is a note only. A random applicant starts near 1 percent (yc_acceptance.md, 0.6 to 2 percent range). Five technical people on an AI agents and trading thesis fit current YC interest, but the pitch is mostly vision and the space includes several YC trading agent companies.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: YC would most plausibly say no because the pitch is a broad vision with no live users or returns, and trading agents for individuals involve regulation and trust questions. Reviewers could also see agent harnesses for trading as a thin layer on top of general model providers.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --years 2022-2025 --industry Fintech --calibration-only (seed 57 percent known, n=23); --years 2018-2021 --industry Fintech (87 percent, n=23); time_to_milestones.csv Fintech months_to_seed p25 3, p50 7, p75 20
anchors.adjustment_reason: The window is 10.4 months from 2026-01-05 to 2026-11-17 and the target is a round above about $1M. Ever reached anchors are about 0.6 to 0.7, and about 60 percent of eventual raisers close within 10 months. A slight plus from a 5 person team and AI plus crypto interest is held to under 1.25 times the windowed figure, and the odds do not rank Instinct against others.

bands.rationale: Small post YC round under $3M from angels or a small fund on top of the YC deal. Angel round from crypto and fintech operators.
Typical institutional seed, near the 2022+ median of 4.1M. Typical seed for an AI trading product with early users.
Upside seed led by a top fund. AI plus crypto and prediction market themes drew large seeds in 2025 and 2026.
Large seed, only with a landmark traction story or a hot thesis. Needs visible assets under management or trading volume growth.

ladder.why_it_fails: A seed above $1M fails to close if the product is a demo with no assets under management, because investors know that agent trading results are hard to verify and that consumer trading apps have heavy regulatory exposure. Crypto market cycles also swing investor appetite. Analogs HyperTrader raised only $1.4M and moved to free access, and Hype and AYC Fund stayed at the YC check or lower.

ladder.why_it_fails: A Series A needs recurring revenue from fees or subscriptions, and consumer trading revenue swings with market volumes. Investors also ask for retention, regulatory clarity and proof that agents add return after costs. Alpaca, a successful YC brokerage API, took a year to reach its $10M A after a $6M seed, with a steady developer customer base that Instinct would lack.

ladder.why_it_fails: A Series B needs a fee business with durable volume through a down market, and many retail trading products lose their users when prices fall. A regulatory action on advice or custody would stop growth, and large brokerages can add agent features to their own apps. SFOX raised a $22.7M A in 2018 then pivoted to institutions, which shows retail routing alone did not carry a B.

ladder.why_it_fails: The company stops before a Series C if retail volumes are cyclical and it never holds regulated licenses that deepen its moat. Brokerages and exchanges can copy agent features with their existing users, and a down crypto market shrinks fee revenue. Alpaca reached its Series C only in 2025, six years after its seed, while most trading companies in the data stayed smaller or were acquired.

outcomes.why_it_fails: Most failures come from the product not proving that its agents beat a simple index or that people keep funds in it. Regulators treat advice and custody seriously, and cycles in crypto kill retail activity. Exits tend to be acqui-hires by exchanges or brokerages under $100M.

killers.risk: Agents do not beat the market after fees, so users leave
killers.evidence: No analog shows persistent retail alpha, and trading apps like HyperTrader moved to free access.
killers.mitigation: Publish verified live results and pick narrow strategies.

killers.risk: Regulation of advice, custody or crypto derivatives
killers.evidence: Retail products that manage money in the US need registration or must stay non custodial, and SFOX and Alpaca built licenses to survive.
killers.mitigation: Stay non custodial and partner with a licensed broker.

killers.risk: Foundation model vendors and brokerages ship agent trading
killers.evidence: Brokerages and exchanges can add agents to apps with existing users and general model labs can offer agent frameworks.
killers.mitigation: Win a niche of onchain markets and own the strategy library.

killers.risk: Crypto cycle downturn cuts retail volumes
killers.evidence: Small crypto trading companies in the data stayed at the YC check or seed after 2022.
killers.mitigation: Support equities and prediction markets as well as crypto.

technical_complexity.rationale: The agents must research thousands of markets, avoid hallucinated trades and manage risk with real money, and a small team must integrate exchanges and onchain venues. Models are available off the shelf, but verified performance and reliability under live conditions are hard.

takeover_risk.rationale: Large trading venues already hold users, data and licenses and can add agent features within a year, though each moves carefully because of regulatory exposure. Model labs could also offer agent harnesses that trade through broker APIs.

evidence.claim: Prediction market volume grew sharply into 2025 and traders are adopting agents, which suggests demand for automation.
Retail trading platforms already earn large fee revenue, which shows spend on tools exists.

roadmap.goal: Live users with real capital and verified performance.
actions: Open a paid beta with 100 or more funded users.
Publish audited live trade logs for the agents.
roadmap.proof: Assets under management or monthly fees that grow for three months in a row.

roadmap.goal: Durable revenue through a market downturn.
actions: Add equities or prediction market venues to reduce crypto dependence.
Secure a licensed partner for custody.
roadmap.proof: Recurring fee revenue that stays within 30 percent of peak in a down month.

brand.name: Instinct
brand.name_check: python3 -I scripts/name_features.py --score "Instinct" --era 2022+ : kind real_word, 8 characters, 2 syllables
strengths: Real word that fits a trading edge story
weaknesses: Generic and hard to own in search
brand.rationale: Instinct is a simple real word like Alpaca or Hype in the same field, and its meaning supports the pitch of better judgment. It is common enough to be hard to search, and it does not decide whether traders trust the product.

narrative.headline: A timely but unproven trading agent vision where a seed above $1M inside 10 months is near the cohort pace and later rounds depend on verified performance.
narrative.general_summary: Instinct builds AI agents that research markets and trade around the clock for individuals. The market for retail trading is large and agent use on prediction markets and onchain venues was rising in 2025, but the pitch is broad and no traction is stated. Retail trading products depend on market cycles and regulation, the nearest YC analogs raised small rounds or stayed at the YC check, and large brokerages can add agents. A seed above $1M inside the 10.4 month window is plausible near the Fintech cohort pace given a five person team. Later rounds depend on proof that the agents earn returns and that users stay. These probabilities do not rank Instinct against others.

assumptions: Blind forecast as of 2026-01-05 using the input file and market searches; results dated after that were ignored.
Window is 10.4 months to 2026-11-17 and seed means an outside round above about $1M.
Anchors use Fintech and B2B calibration cohorts, which are small and right censored for 2022 onward.
